goal: A native `@stacksjs/malware` core package that gives every Stacks app one `scan()` call, one config file and pluggable drivers, so each upload surface in the framework can depend on it instead of inventing its own scanner client.
scope: New package `storage/framework/core/malware` published as `@stacksjs/malware`, with `scan(input, options)` accepting bytes, a ReadableStream, a file path or a file descriptor and returning a Result of `{ verdict: 'clean' | 'infected' | 'suspicious' | 'error', signature?, containerPath?, durationMs }`
Driver `guardian`: in-process scanning through `@zig-utils/anti-virus` (bun:ffi), with a fallback to the zavd Unix socket when configured

Driver `clamd`: the clamd wire protocol (zINSTREAM with 4-byte big-endian frames, zPING, zVERSION) over a Unix socket or TCP. Because zavd speaks the same protocol, this driver covers both clamd and zavd endpoints
Driver `none`: always clean, logged once at boot so a disabled scanner is visible

`MalwareConfig` type in `core/types` and a default `config/malware.ts` overlay: driver, socket path, `failClosed` (default true), max scan bytes, timeout, quarantine disk, and a per-surface switch list (storage, forms, email, ai, file manager)
`health()` for the dashboard and `buddy doctor`
out_of_scope: Wiring the hooks into storage, email and the rest (P8.02 to P8.11)
notes: Fail closed by default: a scanner that cannot answer returns `error`, and callers treat `error` as not clean unless `failClosed: false`
Keep the clamd client streaming: never buffer a whole upload just to frame it
Config follows the overlay rule: `config/malware.ts` merges over defaults, it never replaces them
accept: Unit tests for each driver, including a fake clamd server that answers OK, FOUND and garbage
An EICAR test: `scan()` on the EICAR string returns `infected` through the guardian driver and through the clamd driver pointed at zavd
`failClosed` behaviour covered when the socket is missing
`bun run typecheck` and `./buddy lint` clean

goal: Every file stored through `Storage.put` or `UploadedFile.store*` is scanned after its bytes are read and before anything is written to a disk, so no Stacks app can persist malware through the standard upload API.
scope: Add `scan?: boolean | MalwareScanOptions` to `PutFileOptions`, defaulting to the `storage` switch in `config/malware.ts`
In `putUploadedFile`, call `@stacksjs/malware` between `readBytes` and the optional `transform`, so the original bytes are scanned, not a re-encoded copy
On `infected` or `suspicious`, throw a typed `MalwareDetectedError` carrying the signature name, and hand the bytes to quarantine when P8.08 has landed
`UploadedFile.store` and `storeAs` currently write straight to `Storage.disk().write` and skip `putUploadedFile`; route them through the same scan step
New `UploadedFile.scan()` that returns the verdict without storing, for callers that decide themselves
notes: The scan must run once per stored file, not once per call site: centralise it in a helper both paths use
Return the verdict alongside `PutResult` so callers can persist it
accept: EICAR test: `Storage.put` of an EICAR UploadedFile throws `MalwareDetectedError` and nothing is written to the disk
EICAR test for `store`, `storeAs` and `storePublicly`
A clean file stores exactly as before; existing storage tests stay green
`scan: false` skips scanning and is covered by a test

goal: `Storage.putStream` scans the stream as it flows to the disk, so large uploads are protected without buffering them whole in memory.
scope: Tee the incoming ReadableStream: one branch to the adapter's `putStream`, one to a streaming `@stacksjs/malware` scan (guardian stream handle or clamd INSTREAM)
Write to a temporary key first; promote to the final path only on a clean verdict, delete the temporary object otherwise
Apply back-pressure correctly so a slow scanner slows the upload instead of growing memory
Respect `scan: false` in `PutStreamOptions`
out_of_scope: Presigned uploads that never pass through the server (P8.04)
notes: Adapters that cannot rename cheaply (S3) use copy plus delete for promotion; document the cost
The verdict must be final before the promoted object becomes visible
accept: EICAR test: `putStream` of an EICAR stream leaves no object at the final path on the local and memory adapters
A 200 MB clean stream uploads with bounded memory (asserted in a test with a memory ceiling)
Existing putStream tests green

Optional S3 event notification mode documented for apps that want promotion without a client confirm

notes: Never return the final public URL until promotion; a client must not be able to link to an unscanned object
Lifecycle rule on the staging prefix so abandoned uploads expire

A clean staged object is promoted and its URL resolves

goal: zig-waf can run the Guardian engine as its `@inspectFile` operator in process, so uploads are scanned at the edge without a daemon round trip.
